summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM systems move into production, enabling teams to trace failures, monitor costs, evaluate output quality, and debug complex agent workflows in real time. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on latency regressions, prompt drift, and runaway API spend that can silently erode margins. Tools like LangSmith, Helicone, Langfuse, and Arize have matured into DevOps-grade platforms that bring structured visibility to what were previously opaque model interactions.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, agent and graph-structured workflows, prompt performance, evaluation runs, and human-in-the-loop feedback for LangChain and LangGraph applications
features: Best-in-category trace UI for graph-structured agent workflows
Prompt variant comparison and dataset management
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month; overage ~$2.50 per 1,000 traces. Estimated ~£80/month for typical team usage.
tools.best_for: Teams building production LangChain or LangGraph agents who need deep native tracing and structured evaluation pipelines

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, per-model and per-user costs, latency, token usage, and prompt/response logs via a proxy gateway layer
features: Detailed cost tracking and spend dashboards
Caching and rate limiting to reduce costs
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier: 10K requests/month; Pro: $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team: $799/month (compliance features); Enterprise: custom pricing with SAML SSO and on-prem options. Cheapest managed option at ~£20/month for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing fast setup and granular cost visibility, especially those calling multiple LLM providers and needing immediate spend control

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML experiment tracking, LLM prompt and response logging, model evaluation, fine-tuning runs, and dataset versioning across the full ML lifecycle
features: Prompt management and versioning via W&B Prompts
Integration with major ML frameworks and LLM providers
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; Team plan at $50/seat/month; Enterprise pricing available. Generous free compute hours included on base tier.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams who need unified tracking across both traditional model training and LLM experimentation within a single platform

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, model drift, evaluation metrics, and enterprise-scale telemetry across multi-model deployments
features: RAG retrieval and embedding quality monitoring
Arize Phoenix open-source local version available
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open-source (self-hosted). Managed Arize platform offers a free developer tier; enterprise pricing is custom and contract-based, targeted at large-scale deployments.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams running large-scale or multi-model LLM systems who need rigorous telemetry, RAG quality monitoring, and compliance-grade observability

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, costs, evaluation scores, and user session flows across self-hosted or cloud deployments
features: Native evaluation framework with custom and LLM-as-judge scoring
SDKs for Python, JS, and OpenAI-compatible integrations
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud from ~£20 for 500K requests/month. Self-hosted infrastructure cost ~£30/month with approximately 2 hours of maintenance per month. Most cost-effective overall for high-volume teams.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting open-source flexibility, full data ownership, and a strong balance of tracing, prompt management, and evaluation without vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token consumption, latency, and model interactions via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation across any LLM provider
features: Drop-in SDK for automatic LLM call tracing
Provider-agnostic: works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and more
Exports to any OTel-compatible backend (Jaeger, Grafana, Datadog, etc.)
Minimal code changes required for integration
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Costs are limited to whatever observability backend you export data to (e.g., self-hosted Grafana stack or a commercial APM tool).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams already invested in OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want standardized LLM instrumentation that plugs into their existing observability stack without a new vendor

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination rates, answer relevancy, RAG faithfulness, and regression across 50+ evaluation metrics
features: Regression testing integrated into CI/CD pipelines
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft
tools.pricing: Open-source DeepEval library is free. Confident AI managed platform pricing is not publicly listed; contact for enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams that need the deepest evaluation coverage and want to run automated quality regression tests on LLM outputs before and after deployments

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, per-model and per-session costs, logs, infrastructure metrics, and frontend RUM monitoring in a unified single-deployment platform
features: Unified infrastructure and LLM observability in one tool
Logs, metrics, traces, and RUM in a single deployment
Eliminates need for separate DevOps and LLM telemetry stacks
Open-source with self-hosted and cloud options
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free. Cloud pricing available on request; positioned as cost-efficient relative to running separate specialized stacks.
tools.best_for: Platform and DevOps teams who want to consolidate LLM observability with infrastructure monitoring into a single tool rather than managing multiple specialized platforms

cost_tips: Cache repeated or semantically similar prompts using tools like Helicone's built-in caching or a semantic cache layer such as GPTCache — returning cached responses for near-duplicate queries can cut API spend by 20-40% on high-volume applications

Right-size your model selection by routing simpler queries to cheaper models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini or Haiku) and reserving frontier models only for complex tasks; use observability tools to identify which request types actually need premium models versus where a smaller model performs equally well

Monitor and trim prompt token bloat continuously — use tracing tools like Langfuse or LangSmith to audit your average prompt length per endpoint, then refactor system prompts and few-shot examples to remove redundant instructions, since token costs compound directly with prompt length at scale

Set hard spending alerts and per-user or per-session token budgets using your observability platform; Helicone and LangSmith both support rate limiting and alerting so unexpected traffic spikes or runaway agent loops do not silently exhaust your monthly API budget before you notice
